To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of presenilin‐1 is transiently high in the neuropil at age 5 days in both SAMP1TA and SAMR1 mice and then decreases with postnatal development.
the expression of presenilin‐1, synaptophysin and post‐synaptic protein 95 in the brain of SAMP1TA mice is similar to that of the control strain SAMR1TA mice.

the postnatal changes in the expression and distribution of presenilins and synapse‐associated proteins in the cerebral cortex are similar in senescence‐resistant SAMR1TA/Ngs (SAMP1) and senescence‐susceptible SAMP1TA/ Ngs (SAMR1) mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of synapses in the brain of mice.
the expression of synapses‐related proteins in senescence‐resistant SAMP1TA//Nsg and senescence‐susceptible SAMR1TA/Nsg mice.
a possible role of presenilin proteins in synapse formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of presenilin, synaptophysin and post‐synaptic densities was normal in SAMP1 mice.
presenilin is not involved in the delayed synaptogenesis in SAMP1 mice.

the expression of presenilin, synaptophysin and post‐synaptic protein 95 is not different between the senescence‐resistant and ‐prone strains, but that presenilin is transiently expressed to induce synaptophysin during postnatal development in both strains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
presenilin is not involved in the abnormal development of cognitive function and dendritic spine in the senescence‐resistant strain of mice.

the expression of presenilin and synapse‐associated proteins is not disturbed in SAPP1TA/Ngs, and the delayed formation of dendritic spiny synapses in SAMP1/Ngs is caused by a disturbance in the postnatal regulation of the formation of synapses.
presenilin‐dependent γ‐secretase cleavage of β‐APP and the resulting production of amyloid β‐peptides is not involved in the development of cognitive functions or in dendritic spine formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of presenilin and synapse‐associated proteins was similar in the SAMP1 and SAMR mice.
the postnatal development of the expression of synapses‐related proteins is not different between SAMP1 and SAMR mice.
presenilin expression is transiently high during the early stages of synaptogenesis and then its expression is down‐regulated in the neuropil.
